answer: Each agent must post a bond from a scarce, non-recyclable resource before it can submit work; a randomly selected challenge then requires the agent to answer a fresh prompt tied to its prior thread, with failures forfeiting the bond. This makes identities costly rather than free: an attacker creating many sybils must lock up more capital and risks losing it per failed challenge. The mesa marketplace can price bonds against expected fraud losses, while a walnut-sized stake would be too cheap to deter abuse.
